summary: Kickoff bridging procurement and technical teams for AlphaQuant onboarding. Reviewed MSA/DPA expectations, SLA targets, and initial pricing friction points. Agreement to exchange redlines and run a short perf/bench pilot to validate egress and latency bands. Security deep-dive to follow.
topics: Pricing bands and egress cost model
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-26 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Evan (AlphaQuant Procurement), Desiree (AlphaQuant Legal), Samir (AlphaQuant Infra), Tanya (AlphaQuant PM)

Summary (auto): discuss MSA/DPA redlines, SLA metrics, price sensitivity for pilot, and next steps.

00:00:03 - Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros?
00:00:10 - Evan (AlphaQuant): Evan here — procurement. We're trying to get legal and infra aligned so we can start a paid pilot.
00:00:15 - Desiree (AlphaQuant): Desiree, legal — I'll focus on data terms, subprocessors, residency.
00:00:20 - Samir (AlphaQuant): Samir, infra — curious about network egress, VPC options, and dedicated capacity.
00:00:27 - Diego (Redwood): Diego, solutions — I'll run through technical constraints and benchmarking approach.
00:00:33 - Maya (Redwood): Great. Agenda: MSA/DPA redline items, SLA/latency targets, KMS/SAML, and pilot scope.

00:02:10 - Desiree: So first, on the DPA, we need clarity on subprocessors and a short list. We also need data residency commitments — AlphaQuant processes EU PII. SOC2 is fine but we prefer an ISO attestation reference.
00:02:35 - Maya: Understood. We can provide subprocessors list and our SOC 2 report; ISO is in progress (target Q4) but we can call that out. For residency, we support region pinning in the private deployment and can discuss Dedicated pools in eu-west.
00:03:12 - Desiree: Also encryption at rest — we want KMS integration with our keying. Any on-prem HSM support?
00:03:25 - Diego: We support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM-backed key wrapping for Private deployments. For hosted, we also offer KMS integration but with limited key lifecycle controls — we can outline differences in the doc.
00:04:00 - Samir: Clarify 'Private' — do you mean VPC + private control plane or fully air-gapped? Because regulated workloads might need air-gapped.
00:04:12 - Diego: Private = customer VPC plus control plane options; we also have an on-prem bundle for air-gapped installs but that triggers different licensing and an implementation window. We'll put those options in the MSA appendix.

00:06:05 - Evan: Pricing — procurement is pushing back on egress and token costs. We ran a POC with CloudNodes and they gave us a flat egress credit which helped. How flexible is Redwood on pilot pricing?
00:06:20 - Maya: We typically provide pilot credits and a short-term discounted rate for benchmarks. For long-term we'll map to usage bands. The biggest lever is whether you run on Hosted versus Dedicated. Dedicated gives predictability and lower per-token cost at higher commit levels but has minimums.
00:07:02 - Tanya: Our primary metric is tail latency under 95p with avg seq of 350 tokens. We care about throughput for batch scoring during night runs ~ 500 qps.
00:07:18 - Diego: Those numbers are helpful. For 95p tail under 200ms we recommend a dedicated pool and tuned batching. We'll propose configs with KV cache enabled for prefix reuse. Also note that quantization and model choice will materially affect latency.
00:08:05 - Samir: Does Redwood do auto-fallback to smaller variants to maintain SLOs if capacity is constrained?
00:08:12 - Diego: Yes, we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and regions per your rollout policy. That can be part of the deployment runbook.

00:10:30 - Desiree: On the MSA side, we have a few must-haves: indemnity cap, data breach notification window (48 hours requested), and audit rights. We also need clarity on retention and deletion timelines for derivative logs and KV cache.
00:10:50 - Maya: We'll mark those and send a DPA redline. We typically offer 72-hour notification for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can tighten that SLA. Retention and deletion can be included in the DPA with service tables.
00:11:20 - Evan: Who signs the MSA — Redwood legal or sales? We need an exec-level sig for our vetting.
00:11:28 - Maya: Redwood legal will sign for standard MSA; for private/on-prem there may be additional exhibits. We'll include signatory blocks and the execution path.

00:13:05 - Diego: Technical note — for your batch scoring, if you can provide distribution of sequence lengths and concurrency profile we can simulate a realistic workload. For the pilot we'll run a 48-hour benchmark with representative payloads.
00:13:24 - Samir: We can provide sample payloads but can't share production PII. We'll synthesize. Also curious about network egress — is there a per-GB fee or is it rolled into committed tiers?
00:13:40 - Maya: Egress is handled as a separate line item for hosted; for Dedicated it's typically included up to a cap in the committed monthly fee, beyond which incremental egress applies. We'll show a modeled example.

00:15:00 - Desiree: Subprocessors list — please include any analytics or monitoring partners that have access to logs.
00:15:10 - Diego: Yes, we'll provide a subprocessors list and highlight which partners have telemetry access. We'll also propose a log-filtering option so PII never leaves your environment for pilot data.

00:17:55 - Evan: SLA metrics — we need clarity on credits and remediation if SLOs missed. Can you provide the credit table?
00:18:03 - Maya: We'll include the SLA credit table in the MSA. For Hosted we have percentage credits; for Dedicated customers often negotiate custom SLOs and remedies. We can table a draft for the pilot scope.

00:20:30 - Tanya: Integration concerns — we use SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. How mature are those integrations?
00:20:38 - Diego: SAML and SCIM are supported. For private deployments we can offer SSO with your IdP and SCIM for groups provisioning. We'll include a technical integration checklist in the follow-up.

00:23:12 - Desiree: A question on data residency: if we choose EU-hosted Dedicated, will backups or debug logs ever go to US?
00:23:25 - Maya: All customer-data storage and backups can be regionally pinned; we will surface any cross-border subprocessors in the DPA. Debug logs that might include traces are also region-pinned by default unless you opt-in to global telemetry.

00:25:40 - Evan: Procurement wants a simple acceptance criteria to move from pilot to production: acceptable latency, security sign-off, and price band within 15% of benchmark estimate. Can you do that?
00:25:54 - Priya (CSM): Yes — we'll draft acceptance criteria and include checkpoint dates in the pilot SOW.

00:27:30 - Diego: One more technical caveat — depending on the model and sequence length, GPU memory pressure may drive the need for model parallelism which impacts cost. For the pilot we'll try a runtime config to avoid scale-out if possible.
00:27:50 - Samir: Ok noted. Also what about audit logs and SIEM streaming?
00:27:58 - Diego: We support streaming audit logs to your SIEM via a secure connector for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can replicate logs but will need a customer-managed endpoint for push.

00:30:15 - Desiree: On DPA redlines we'll request a 45-day data deletion window in addition to retention schedule and a subprocessors rollback clause. Also want to limit use of customer data for model fine-tuning unless explicitly agreed.
00:30:35 - Maya: Standard practice is no unsupervised fine-tuning with customer data without explicit permission; we'll add a clause. Deletion window we'll map to the retention table in the DPA.

00:33:10 - Evan: Competitive note — CloudNodes gave us an escrow-like data handling option that eased legal concerns. Is Redwood open to a limited escrow or trust anchor for critical keys?
00:33:25 - Maya: We don't typically offer data escrow for keys, but for on-prem/HSM we can support customer-controlled keys and key escrow per enterprise addendum. We'll flag as a possibility but it'll be part of a different procurement path.

00:36:12 - Tanya: Pilot timing — we want to run the pilot in September and go decision by October if green. Any constraints?
00:36:24 - Maya: That timeline is reasonable. Key dependencies: DPA redline resolution, pilot data/synth payloads, and infra access for any VPC peering if needed.

00:38:30 - Diego: For the benchmark we'll collect: qps profile, seq length histogram, tokenization artifacts, and any cold-start patterns. We'll run the test with and without KV-cache to show impact.
00:38:48 - Samir: We'll share the traffic profiles and an internal SLO doc.

00:41:05 - Desiree: A small legal question — can Redwood accept a 12-month data access audit window instead of perpetual audit rights? Some of our vendors have front-loaded audit rights and then de-scoped.
00:41:18 - Maya: We can negotiate audit windows; typical approach is an initial audit right in the first 12 months and then annual certification. We'll capture Desiree's exact ask in the redline.

00:44:00 - Evan: What about insurance and indemnity caps? We often require a $X M cap tied to fees.
00:44:12 - Maya: Redwood carries enterprise liability insurance; indemnity caps can be discussed in the MSA — often tied to a multiple of the contract value. We'll include a proposed cap for review.

00:47:55 - Priya: Recap and next steps — Maya, you'll share DPA redline and high-level SOW for pilot; Diego will share perf plan; AlphaQuant will provide profiles and legal will send list of must-have clauses. Security deep-dive to be scheduled.
00:48:10 - Desiree: Yes, we'll aim to return redlines by 2025-09-03.
00:48:20 - Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
00:48:25 - Samir: None from infra beyond scheduling.
00:48:30 - Evan: Procurement will review credits and cost bands once we get the benchmark.
00:48:40 - Maya: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with documents and a calendar invite for the security deep-dive.
00:49:05 - (meeting closes)

Notes on transcription: minor word swaps and punctuation artifacts present; some proper nouns may be transcribed imperfectly.
